subject: POC hands-on kickoff & environment checklist
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: POC hands-on kickoff & environment checklist

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the time last week. We’re excited to get the hands-on POC started. Proposed objective for the kickoff session: validate prompt variants, routing rules, and run a couple of short load checks against a staging endpoint so you can verify latency/cost profiles for representative queries. Estimated session length: 90 minutes.

Three slot options (PT):
- Thu May 14 — 10:00–11:30 AM PT
- Thu May 14 — 2:00–3:30 PM PT
- Fri May 15 — 9:00–10:30 AM PT

Pre-kickoff asks (to make the session productive):
- Can you confirm which participants will be on the call and whether procurement needs to join?
- Do you need us to provision a sandbox account or provide API keys ahead of time? We can create a scoped sandbox key.
- If your environment is behind a VPC, we’ll need an allowlist of outbound IPs — I’ve attached a small text file with the Redwood staging egress addresses we’ll use.
- Any specific prompt samples or routing rules you want us to test during the session? If you can drop a short list, Rishi will build a mini-bench.

Attached: redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (agenda + environment checklist).

If none of the slots work, tell us preferred windows and we’ll adjust.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0131

Jordan —

Thanks, the agenda looks good. We can do Thu May 14 10:00 AM PT. Attendees: me (Alicia), Diego Ramos (engineering lead), and I looped in procurement for contracting/POC approval (procurement@acmehealth.com).

We will need a sandbox account + scoped API key in advance so our security team can scan the traffic. Also, please send the staging endpoints and any TLS/hostnames so we can add them to our internal allowlist.

Prompt set: I’ll upload 6 representative prompts to the shared Drive folder by EOD. For routing, we primarily want: 1) patient-data-safe path (PII redaction check), 2) long-form summarization path. If you can route those two during the run that’d be ideal.

Thanks — looking forward to it.
Alicia

agomez@acmehealth.com

Subject: Action items — Acme POC: sandbox keys, endpoints, and prompt bank

Team —

Alicia confirmed Thu May 14 at 10:00 AM PT. Attendees include Acme product + eng and procurement. Please see the immediate tasks so we’re ready before the kickoff: 

1) Sandbox API key & account
- Marissa: can you create a scoped sandbox API key for ACME with the following constraints: generation-only key (expires in 14 days), scopes: text.generate, chat.stream, embeddings.read. Tag with deal_id=RDW-ACME-2026-001 and environment=staging. Send the key stub to Alicia and me (do not post to shared Drive).

2) Staging endpoints and network allowlist
- Marissa / Ops: publish the staging hostname + TLS cert info and confirm egress IP addresses. I attached network-allowlist.txt with the five egress IPs we expect; if those change, call it out.

3) Prompt bank + routing config
- Rishi: prepare a short prompt bank (6 prompts from Acme’s Drive) and a basic routing policy that exercises: patient-data-safe path with redaction hook, and long-form summarization path. Also add a 30-second load test script that sends batched requests to the summarization path (~50 concurrent virtual users for ~60s) so we can show tail latency.

4) Demo collateral + runbook
- Tessa: update the kickoff slide deck with the quick checklist and add step-by-step runbook bullets for the session (who shares screens, when we switch to load test, fallback plan if staging is throttled).

Deadline: please confirm completion by EOD Mon May 12 so procurement can start paperwork if needed.

Attachments: network-allowlist.txt, sandbox-instructions.md (draft).

Thanks — Jordan
